t: Apex Identity Command Nexus: Single-Authority Protocol — Simple
name: Apex Identity Command Nexus: Single-Authority Protocol — Simple
title: Apex Identity Command Nexus: Single-Authority Protocol — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] A protocol that guarantees exactly one decider per decision: authority is delegated in writing, conflicts escalate by rule, and the decider's identity is logged with the decision. Ambiguity collapses to a name.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Delegation-change quorum for 9 = 5 votes. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.
chapter_source: The Apex Identity Command Nexus (AICN) — Command Collapse vs. The Fixed Absolute Finality
real_world_basis: RACI-style authority with logged decisions is standard in incident command.
signature_version: Signature version: the command-collapse protocol — the chapter's Command Collapse as a protocol that always resolves to one accountable decider, with the 'absolute finality' framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: write the delegation chart first, log every decision's decider, and rehearse escalations.
math_note: Delegation-change quorum for 9: 5 votes [verified]; Escalation path: 3 stages x 200 ms: 600 ms [verified]
safety: Accountability safety: the decider is named on every decision — 'the system decided' is never an acceptable log entry.
how_it_works: Decisions feed the authority resolver; the protocol names the decider per the delegation chart. The demo recomputes the quorum for delegation changes and the latency of the escalation path.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub
Speculative = Signature-labeled, never as established fact

t: Apex Identity Command Nexus: Finality Verifier — Simple
name: Apex Identity Command Nexus: Finality Verifier — Simple
title: Apex Identity Command Nexus: Finality Verifier — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] A verifier that proves a command decision is final and legitimate: it checks the authority chain, the quorum, and the log integrity, then certifies. Final means verified, not just declared.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Decision-log collision odds, 15M in 64 bits = 6.099e-06 probability. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.
chapter_source: The Apex Identity Command Nexus (AICN) — Command Collapse vs. The Fixed Absolute Finality
real_world_basis: Decision certification is standard in financial and safety-critical systems.
signature_version: Signature version: the finality verifier — the chapter's Fixed Absolute Finality as a verified certification, with the 'absolute' framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: define finality criteria first, verify every decision, and publish certifications.
math_note: Decision-log collision odds, 15M in 64 bits: 6.099e-06 probability [verified]; Decision entropy at p=0.5: 1.0000 bits [verified]
safety: Legitimacy safety: the verifier can refuse certification — and its refusals are logged too.
how_it_works: Decisions feed the verifier; chain, quorum, and log check out; certification issues. The demo recomputes the collision odds for the decision log and the entropy of the decision distribution.

standards: Full-file record, never a stub
